second_order: making, inhabiting, and undoing the Galaxy91122/Paul Byron prank
theme_note: These codes belong together because people collectively make the subreddit into Galaxy91122 and Paul Byron, play along or push back, and then revert the one-day joke; what varies is whether they launch, notice, impersonate, praise, resist, or clean it up. This is the room own April Fools conduct, not the canvas.

second_order: trying to get the first Habs C onto the canvas
theme_note: These passages are the first canvas call and the practical replies that leave another drawing, fail to locate the C, or report placing its outline and red pixels; they share an attempt to make the initial Habs mark while varying between recruitment, confusion, and placement.

second_order: fooling each other with a Price-season headline
theme_note: These three turns form one bounded prank practice: posting a false season-over headline, being frightened despite recognizing it, and admitting the date eventually gave the joke away. It varies between bait, reaction, and explanation and is the room own April Fools conduct, not canvas work.

These codes hold together as attempts to alter, shrink, relabel, or return to the Leafs canvas mark; what varies is the joke inserted, the pixel strategy, persistence against repair, and sequencing it after guarding the Habs logo.

second_order: building and moving the Habs logo one pixel at a time
theme_note: These passages share practical construction of the Habs mark: taking space, publishing coordinates, placing pixels, rotating accounts, negotiating a route around a neighbour, relocating, and explaining how pixel cooperation works. They vary from recruitment and plans to individual labour and finding the new site.

second_order: turning hockey rivals and other rooms into allies
theme_note: These passages try to enlarge the side that can sustain the drawings by preferring rival logos to none, recasting hockey as one side, asking r/Kanye and hockey clubs for help, arguing rivals must cooperate, and recounting politicking across subreddits and Discords. What varies is the proposed partner and whether the alliance is a request, justification, or retrospective claim.

second_order: calling out attacks and trying to keep the CH alive
theme_note: These codes belong together as defence under pressure: naming attackers, warning the logo is threatened, spending moves to keep it alive, judging resources insufficient, vowing defence, and then reporting that the void swallowed it. What varies is attributed attacker, urgency, persistence, and whether the speaker diagnoses survival or loss.

second_order: joking that an outnumbered pixel fight sums up life
theme_note: This single exchange turn belongs with no broader practice in the pool: it converts another helper account of being overwhelmed four-to-one into a joke about the speaker life.

second_order: celebrating that Reddit did it while the logo still needs work
theme_note: These passages claim a shared success and describe having pulled through or reached a perfect logo; what varies is terse image-post celebration versus commenters naming the achievement. The later maintenance codes remain elsewhere, so the theme preserves victory as a milestone rather than a settled endpoint.

second_order: trying to keep an un-griefed record of the canvas
theme_note: This single code asks for a clean screenshot to become a sidebar post after continued damage, a distinct practice of preserving the outcome rather than placing or defending pixels.

second_order: trying to add a Stanley Cup without taking over neighbours
theme_note: These codes all work through where and how to begin a Cup drawing: placing its first pixel, choosing a lower or messy site, asking for chat and a guide, refusing to overwrite Serbia, MIT, or McGill, disputing that restraint, and responding to displaced neighbours. The variation is between construction, siting, restraint, and resistance; the proposed Cup is not shown completed.

second_order: arguing over r/place flooding the Habs board
theme_note: These passages share a forum-level dispute over how much canvas talk belongs here: asking for consolidation, defending the short event and collective contribution, accepting a megathread, calling the posts spam, broadening the complaint to memes and style, and finally returning to playoff worries once r/place is over.

second_order: warning that Buffalo might turn the sax into a chicken wing
theme_note: This surviving title is a single-code theme because the warning has no body or replies to connect it to a larger practice without speculation.

second_order: drawing the line around low-effort shitposts
theme_note: These codes belong together as the room debates and applies a moderation practice: distinguishing posts from comments, exceptional memes from routine repeats, discretionary allowances from blanket bans, and asking whether recent r/place posts fall under the stance. What varies is rule-setting, requests for exceptions, mockery, and participant acceptance or complaint.

second_order: recounting an intact but messy canvas finish
theme_note: These post-event passages make the community first account of its outcome: marking the logo and Beliveau homage intact, remembering defence through work, joking about 81 Faige, noticing changes, attributing attacks, and correcting a claim of spontaneous creation with chat coordination. They vary between commemoration, labour memory, joking alteration, blame, and origin correction.

second_order: telling destroyers to make their own logo
theme_note: These contrary-search turns share a rival response that redirects Habs participants from damaging another mark toward creating their own; what varies is whether the redirection is a blunt insult, a retaliatory threat, or a create-not-destroy appeal.
